q: The Slepian–Wolf theorem says two correlated sources X and Y can be separately encoded (without communication) and jointly decoded at rates:
opts: R_X ≥ H(X|Y), R_Y ≥ H(Y|X), R_X+R_Y ≥ H(X,Y)
exp: Slepian–Wolf: separate encoding suffices — no communication needed during encoding. The rate region is: R_X ≥ H(X|Y), R_Y ≥ H(Y|X), R_X+R_Y ≥ H(X,Y). This is remarkable: the rate achievable equals the distributed Shannon rate.
